22: #define BK7258_IPI_SCHED        (1u << 0)
23: #define BK7258_IPI_CALL         (1u << 1)
24: #define BK7258_IPI_RETRY_LIMIT  1024
25: 
26: #define BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_NOTIFY (BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK + 1u)
27: #define BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_PING   (BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK + 2u)
28: #define BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_ACK    (BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK + 3u)

33: static atomic_t g_ipi_pending[CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS];

37: static int bk7258_smp_boot_send(int cpu, uint32_t command)
38: {
39:   uint32_t data[2] = {command, 0};
40:   int retry;
41: 
42:   UP_DMB();
43:   for (retry = 0; retry < BK7258_IPI_RETRY_LIMIT; retry++)
44:     {
45:       int ret = bk7258_mbox_send((uint8_t)(cpu + 1), data);
46: 
47:       if (ret == OK)
48:         {
49:           return OK;
50:         }
51: 
52:       if (ret != -EAGAIN)
53:         {
54:           return ret;
55:         }
56: 
57:       __asm__ volatile("nop");
58:     }
59: 
60:   return -ETIMEDOUT;
61: }

63: static int bk7258_smp_kick(int cpu, uint32_t pending)
64: {
65:   uint32_t data[2] = {BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK, 0};
66:   int expected = 0;
67:   int retry;
68: 
69:   if ((unsigned int)cpu >= CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS || cpu == this_cpu())
70:     {
71:       return -EINVAL;
72:     }
73: 
74:   atomic_or_release(&g_ipi_pending[cpu], pending);
75:   if (!atomic_cmpxchg_acquire(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], &expected, 1))
76:     {
77:       return OK;
78:     }
79: 
80:   UP_DMB();
81:   for (retry = 0; retry < BK7258_IPI_RETRY_LIMIT; retry++)
82:     {
83:       int ret = bk7258_mbox_send((uint8_t)(cpu + 1), data);
84: 
85:       if (ret == OK)
86:         {
87:           return OK;
88:         }
89: 
90:       if (ret != -EAGAIN)
91:         {
92:           atomic_set_release(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], 0);
93:           return ret;
94:         }
95: 
96:       __asm__ volatile("nop");
97:     }
98: 
99:   atomic_set_release(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], 0);
100:   return -ETIMEDOUT;
101: }

103: void bk7258_smp_ipi_receive(int irq, void *context, uint32_t command)
104: {
105:   int cpu = this_cpu();
106: 
107:   if (command == BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_NOTIFY)
108:     {
109:       if (cpu == 0)
110:         {
111:           g_boot_seen |= BK7258_BOOT_SEEN_NOTIFY;
112:         }
113: 
114:       return;
115:     }
116: 
117:   if (command == BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_PING)
118:     {
119:       if (cpu == 1 &&
120:           bk7258_smp_boot_send(0, BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_ACK) < 0)
121:         {
122:           PANIC();
123:         }
124: 
125:       bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ACK);
126:       return;
127:     }
128: 
129:   if (command == BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_ACK)
130:     {
131:       if (cpu == 0)
132:         {
133:           g_boot_seen |= BK7258_BOOT_SEEN_ACK;
134:         }
135: 
136:       return;
137:     }
138: 
139:   if (command != BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK)
140:     {
141:       return;
142:     }
143: 
144:   for (;;)
145:     {
146:       uint32_t pending = atomic_xchg_acquire(&g_ipi_pending[cpu], 0);
147: 
148:       if ((pending & BK7258_IPI_CALL) != 0)
149:         {
150:           nxsched_smp_call_handler(irq, context, NULL);
151:         }
152: 
153:       if ((pending & BK7258_IPI_SCHED) != 0)
154:         {
155:           nxsched_process_delivered(cpu);
156:         }
157: 
158:       atomic_set_release(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], 0);
159:       UP_DMB();
160:       if (atomic_read_acquire(&g_ipi_pending[cpu]) == 0)
161:         {
162:           break;
163:         }
164: 
165:       atomic_set_release(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], 1);
166:     }
167: }

30: #if CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS != 2
31: #  error "BK7258 OpenVela SMP supports exactly two AP CPUs"
32: #endif
33: 
34: #if CONFIG_BK7258_CPU_FREQ_HZ != 480000000
35: #  error "BK7258 OpenVela SMP requires the fixed 480 MHz CP contract"
36: #endif
37: 
38: #define BK7258_CPU2_ONLINE_CYCLES  (CONFIG_BK7258_CPU_FREQ_HZ / 2u)
39: #define BK7258_CPU2_POLL_LIMIT     4000000u
40: 
41: extern uint8_t __secondary_vectors_start[];
42: extern uint8_t __secondary_boot_stack_base[];
43: 
44: static void bk7258_cpu2_hold_reset(void)
45: {
46:   putreg32(getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL) & ~BK7258_CPU2_RESET_RELEASE,
47:            BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL);
48:   UP_DSB();
49: }
50: 
51: static void bk7258_cpu2_release_reset(void)
52: {
53:   putreg32(getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL) | BK7258_CPU2_RESET_RELEASE,
54:            BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL);
55:   UP_DSB();
56:   __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
57: }
58: 
59: static void __attribute__((used, noreturn)) bk7258_secondary_idle(void)
60: {
61:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_IDLE);
62:   arm_initialize_stack();
63:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_STACK);
64:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ONLINE);
65:   bk7258_smp_boot_notify();
66:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_NOTIFY);
67:   up_irq_enable();
68:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_IRQ_ON);
69:   sched_note_cpu_started(this_task());
70:   nx_idle_trampoline();
71:   PANIC();
72: }
73: 
74: static void __attribute__((naked, noreturn))
75: bk7258_secondary_enter(uintptr_t idle_top __attribute__((unused)),
76:                        uintptr_t idle_base __attribute__((unused)))
77: {
78:   __asm__ volatile
79:     (
80:       "msr psp, r0\n"
81: #ifdef CONFIG_ARMV8M_STACKCHECK_HARDWARE
82:       "msr psplim, r1\n"
83: #endif
84:       "mrs r1, control\n"
85:       "orr r1, r1, #2\n"
86:       "msr control, r1\n"
87:       "isb sy\n"
88:       "b bk7258_secondary_idle\n"
89:     );
90: }
91: 
92: static void __attribute__((used, noinline, noreturn,
93:                            target("general-regs-only")))
94: bk7258_secondary_boot(void)
95: {
96:   struct tcb_s *tcb;
97:   uintptr_t idle_top;
98: 
99:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ENTRY);
100:   bk7258_cpu_private_initialize(false);
101:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_PRIVATE);
102:   bk7258_irqinitialize_secondary();
103:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_IRQ);
104:   if (bk7258_mbox_secondary_init() < 0)
105:     {
106:       PANIC();
107:     }
108: 
109:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX);
110: 
111:   tcb = current_task(1);
112:   idle_top = ((uintptr_t)tcb->stack_base_ptr + tcb->adj_stack_size) & ~7u;
113:   bk7258_secondary_enter(idle_top, (uintptr_t)tcb->stack_base_ptr);
114: }
115: 
116: void __attribute__((naked, noreturn, section(".start_text")))
117: bk7258_secondary_start(void)
118: {
119:   __asm__ volatile
120:     (
121:       "cpsid i\n"
122:       "movs r0, #1\n"
123:       "ldr r1, =0x20000000\n"
124:       "str r0, [r1]\n"
125:       "ldr r0, =__secondary_boot_stack_base\n"
126:       "msr msplim, r0\n"
127:       "b bk7258_secondary_boot\n"
128:     );
129: }
130: 
131: int up_cpu_start(int cpu)
132: {
133:   irqstate_t flags;
134:   uint32_t started;
135:   uint32_t polls = 0;
136:   uint32_t control;
137:   uint32_t status;
138:   bool ping_sent = false;
139: 
140:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_ENTER);
141: 
142:   if (cpu != 1 || this_cpu() != 0)
143:     {
144:       return -EINVAL;
145:     }
146: 
147:   status = getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS);
148:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, status);
149:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, bk7258_mbox_smp_ready());
150:   if ((status & BK7258_CPU_STATUS_CPU2_POWER_DOWN) != 0 ||
151:       !bk7258_mbox_smp_ready())
152:     {
153:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "CPU2 prerequisite failed: status=%08lx mbox=%u\n",
154:              (unsigned long)status, bk7258_mbox_smp_ready());
155:       PANIC();
156:     }
157: 
158:   bk7258_cpu2_hold_reset();
159:   control = getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL);
160:   status = getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS);
161:   if ((control & BK7258_CPU2_RESET_RELEASE) != 0 ||
162:       (status & BK7258_CPU_STATUS_CPU2_RESET) != 0)
163:     {
164:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "CPU2 reset hold failed: ctrl=%08lx status=%08lx\n",
165:              (unsigned long)control, (unsigned long)status);
166:       PANIC();
167:     }
168: 
169:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_HELD);
170:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, control);
171:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, status);
172: 
173:   bk7258_smp_prepare_boot();
174:   putreg32(0, BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN0);
175:   putreg32(0, BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN1);
176:   modifyreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL, BK7258_CPU2_OFFSET_MASK,
177:               BK7258_CPU2_RXEVT_SEL |
178:               (((uintptr_t)__secondary_vectors_start >> 8) <<
179:                BK7258_CPU2_OFFSET_SHIFT));
180:   UP_DMB();
181:   UP_DSB();
182: 
183:   putreg32(getreg32(NVIC_DEMCR) | NVIC_DEMCR_TRCENA, NVIC_DEMCR);
184:   putreg32(0, DWT_CYCCNT);
185:   putreg32(getreg32(DWT_CTRL) | DWT_CTRL_CYCCNTENA_MASK, DWT_CTRL);
186:   started = getreg32(DWT_CYCCNT);
187:   flags = up_irq_save();
188:   bk7258_cpu2_release_reset();
189:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_RELEASED);
190:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL));
191:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS));
192: 
193:   while (!bk7258_smp_boot_test_complete())
194:     {
195:       bk7258_mbox_kick_rx();
196:       if (bk7258_smp_boot_notified() && !ping_sent)
197:         {
198:           if (bk7258_smp_boot_ping(1) < 0)
199:             {
200:               break;
201:             }
202: 
203:           ping_sent = true;
204:           bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_ONLINE);
205:         }
206: 
207:       if (getreg32(DWT_CYCCNT) - started >= BK7258_CPU2_ONLINE_CYCLES ||
208:           ++polls >= BK7258_CPU2_POLL_LIMIT)
209:         {
210:           break;
211:         }
212:     }
213: 
214:   if (!bk7258_smp_boot_test_complete())
215:     {
216:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL));
217:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS));
218:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH1_STATUS));
219:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(3, getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH2_STATUS));
220:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(4, ping_sent);
221:       bk7258_cpu2_hold_reset();
222:       up_irq_restore(flags);
223:       syslog(LOG_ERR,
224:              "CPU2 online timeout: ctrl=%08lx status=%08lx fifo=%08lx/%08lx ping=%u\n",
225:              (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL),
226:              (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS),
227:              (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH1_STATUS),
228:              (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH2_STATUS), ping_sent);
229:       PANIC();
230:     }
231: 
232:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_IPI_DONE);
233:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, UINT32_MAX);
234:   putreg32(1u << (BK7258_EXTIRQ_MAILBOX & 31),
235:            NVIC_IRQ_CLRPEND(BK7258_EXTIRQ_MAILBOX));
236:   UP_DSB();
237:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_IRQ_RESTORE);
238:   up_irq_restore(flags);
239:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_IRQ_RETURN);
240:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_START_DONE);
241:   return OK;
242: }

115:   UP_DSB();
116:   UP_ISB();
117: 
118:   putreg32(0, BK7258_SAU_BASE + 0x08);
119:   putreg32(0x00000000u, BK7258_SAU_BASE + 0x0c);
120:   putreg32(0x0fffffe3u, BK7258_SAU_BASE + 0x10);
121:   putreg32(1, BK7258_SAU_BASE + 0x08);
122:   putreg32(0x10000000u, BK7258_SAU_BASE + 0x0c);
123:   putreg32(0xefffffe1u, BK7258_SAU_BASE + 0x10);
124:   putreg32(1, BK7258_SAU_BASE + 0x00);
125:   UP_DSB();
126:   UP_ISB();

129:   UP_DSB();
130:   UP_ISB();

132: #ifdef CONFIG_ARM_MPU
133:   {

136:       MPU_TYPE_DREGION_SHIFT;

143:           }
144:       }

155: static void __attribute__((used, noinline, noreturn,
156:                            target("general-regs-only")))
157: bk7258_start(void)
158: {
159:   const uint8_t *src;
160:   uint8_t *dest;
161: 
162:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_PRIMARY_C);
163: 
164:   /* Enable CP10/CP11 before code compiled for the hard-float ABI can use the
165:    * floating-point extension.
166:    */
167: 
168:   /* modifyreg32() uses a BSS-backed spinlock.  SRAM is retained across an
169:    * AP-only reset, so it must not be used before this function clears BSS.
170:    */
171: 
172:   putreg32(getreg32(NVIC_CPACR) |
173:            NVIC_CPACR_CP_FULL(10) | NVIC_CPACR_CP_FULL(11), NVIC_CPACR);
174:   UP_DSB();
175:   UP_ISB();
176:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_PRIMARY_CPACR);

198:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_PRIMARY_VECTORS);

1033:

1035:

1038:

1048:     }

1098: 			case SMP_DWT_SYNC_WATCHPOINT:

1114: 	return;

220:         "	tst lr, #0x10									\n"/* Test Bit[4] in LR. Bit[4] of EXC_RETURN is 0 if the FPU is in use. */
221:         "	it eq											\n"
222:         "	vstmdbeq r0!, {s16-s31}							\n"/* Store the FPU registers which are not saved automatically. */
223: #endif /* configENABLE_FPU */
224: #if ( configENABLE_MPU == 1 )
225:         "	mrs r1, psplim									\n"/* r1 = PSPLIM. */
226:         "	mrs r2, control									\n"/* r2 = CONTROL. */
227:         "	mov r3, lr										\n"/* r3 = LR/EXC_RETURN. */
228:         "	stmdb r0!, {r1-r11}								\n"/* Store on the stack - PSPLIM, CONTROL, LR and registers that are not automatically saved. */
229: #else /* configENABLE_MPU */
230:         "	mrs r2, psplim									\n"/* r2 = PSPLIM. */
231:         "	mov r3, lr										\n"/* r3 = LR/EXC_RETURN. */
232:         "	stmdb r0!, {r2-r11}								\n"/* Store on the stack - PSPLIM, LR and registers that are not automatically saved. */
233: #endif /* configENABLE_MPU */
234:         "													\n"
235:         "   ldr r2, xCoreId                                 \n"
236:         "   ldr r2, [r2]                                    \n"/* r2 = core id */
237:         "	ldr r1, pxCurrentTCBsConst						\n"
238:         "   ldr r1, [r1, r2, lsl #2]                        \n"/* r1 = pxCurrentTCBs[portGET_CORE_ID()] */
239:         "	str r0, [r1]									\n"/* Save the new top of stack in TCB. */
240:         "													\n"
241: //        "	mov r0, %0										\n"/* r0 = configMAX_SYSCALL_INTERRUPT_PRIORITY */
242: //        "	msr basepri, r0									\n"/* Disable interrupts upto configMAX_SYSCALL_INTERRUPT_PRIORITY. */
243: //        "	dsb												\n"
244: //        "	isb												\n"
245:         "   mov r0, r2                                      \n"/* r0 = core id*/
246:         "	bl vTaskSwitchContext							\n"
247: //        "	mov r0, #0										\n"/* r0 = 0. */
248: //        "	msr basepri, r0									\n"/* Enable interrupts. */
249:         "													\n"
250:         "   ldr r2, xCoreId                                 \n"
251:         "   ldr r2, [r2]                                    \n"/* r2 = core id */
252:         "	ldr r1, pxCurrentTCBsConst						\n"
253:         "   ldr r1, [r1, r2, lsl #2]                        \n"/* r1 = pxCurrentTCBs[portGET_CORE_ID()] */
254:         "	ldr r0, [r1]									\n"/* The first item in pxCurrentTCB is the task top of stack. r0 now points to the top of stack. */
255:         "													\n"
256: #if ( configENABLE_MPU == 1 )
257:         "	dmb												\n"/* Complete outstanding transfers before disabling MPU. */
258:         "	ldr r2, xMPUCTRLConst							\n"/* r2 = 0xe000ed94 [Location of MPU_CTRL]. */
259:         "	ldr r4, [r2]									\n"/* Read the value of MPU_CTRL. */
260:         "	bic r4, #1										\n"/* r4 = r4 & ~1 i.e. Clear the bit 0 in r4. */
261:         "	str r4, [r2]									\n"/* Disable MPU. */
262:         "													\n"
263:         "	adds r1, #4										\n"/* r1 = r1 + 4. r1 now points to MAIR0 in TCB. */
264:         "	ldr r3, [r1]									\n"/* r3 = *r1 i.e. r3 = MAIR0. */
265:         "	ldr r2, xMAIR0Const								\n"/* r2 = 0xe000edc0 [Location of MAIR0]. */
266:         "	str r3, [r2]									\n"/* Program MAIR0. */
267:         "	ldr r2, xRNRConst								\n"/* r2 = 0xe000ed98 [Location of RNR]. */
268:         "	movs r3, #4										\n"/* r3 = 4. */
269:         "	str r3, [r2]									\n"/* Program RNR = 4. */
270:         "	adds r1, #4										\n"/* r1 = r1 + 4. r1 now points to first RBAR in TCB. */
271:         "	ldr r2, xRBARConst								\n"/* r2 = 0xe000ed9c [Location of RBAR]. */
272:         "	ldmia r1!, {r4-r11}								\n"/* Read 4 sets of RBAR/RLAR registers from TCB. */
273:         "	stmia r2!, {r4-r11}								\n"/* Write 4 set of RBAR/RLAR registers using alias registers. */
274:         "													\n"
275:         "	ldr r2, xMPUCTRLConst							\n"/* r2 = 0xe000ed94 [Location of MPU_CTRL]. */
276:         "	ldr r4, [r2]									\n"/* Read the value of MPU_CTRL. */
277:         "	orr r4, #1										\n"/* r4 = r4 | 1 i.e. Set the bit 0 in r4. */
278:         "	str r4, [r2]									\n"/* Enable MPU. */
279:         "	dsb												\n"/* Force memory writes before continuing. */
280: #endif /* configENABLE_MPU */
281:         "													\n"
282: #if ( configENABLE_MPU == 1 )
283:         "	ldmia r0!, {r1-r11}								\n"/* Read from stack - r1 = PSPLIM, r2 = CONTROL, r3 = LR and r4-r11 restored. */
284: #else /* configENABLE_MPU */
285:         "	ldmia r0!, {r2-r11}								\n"/* Read from stack - r2 = PSPLIM, r3 = LR and r4-r11 restored. */
286: #endif /* configENABLE_MPU */
287:         "													\n"
288: #if ( configENABLE_FPU == 1 )
289:         "	tst r3, #0x10									\n"/* Test Bit[4] in LR. Bit[4] of EXC_RETURN is 0 if the FPU is in use. */
290:         "	it eq											\n"
291:         "	vldmiaeq r0!, {s16-s31}							\n"/* Restore the FPU registers which are not restored automatically. */
292: #endif /* configENABLE_FPU */
293:         "													\n"
294: #if ( configENABLE_MPU == 1 )
295:         "	msr psplim, r1									\n"/* Restore the PSPLIM register value for the task. */
296:         "	msr control, r2									\n"/* Restore the CONTROL register value for the task. */
297: #else /* configENABLE_MPU */
298:         "	msr psplim, r2									\n"/* Restore the PSPLIM register value for the task. */
299: #endif /* configENABLE_MPU */
300:         "	msr psp, r0										\n"/* Remember the new top of stack for the task. */
301:         "	bx r3											\n"
302:         "													\n"
303:         "	.align 4										\n"
304:         "pxCurrentTCBsConst: .word pxCurrentTCBs			\n"
305:         "xCoreId: .word 0x20000000                          \n"
306: #if ( configENABLE_MPU == 1 )
307:         "xMPUCTRLConst: .word 0xe000ed94					\n"

44: uint32_t rtos_get_time_diff(void) {
45: #if CONFIG_AON_RTC || CONFIG_ANA_RTC
46: 	//uint64_t cur_aon_time = bk_aon_rtc_get_us()/1000;
47: 	uint64_t cur_aon_time = bk_aon_rtc_get_ms();
48: 	uint32_t cur_os_time = rtos_get_time(); //ms
49: 	uint64_t diff_time = (cur_aon_time - base_aon_time); //ms
50: 	uint32_t diff_ms = 0;
51: 
52: 	if((uint32_t)(diff_time >> 32) & 0x7FF0000) {
53: 		BK_LOGD(TAG, "aon_rtc overfollow....\r\n");
54: 		BK_DUMP_OUT("diff time: 0x%x:0x%08x\r\n", (u32)(diff_time >> 32), (u32)(diff_time & 0xFFFFFFFF));
55: 		return 0;
56: 	}
57: 
58: 	if(cur_os_time >= base_os_time) {
59: 		if (diff_time + base_os_time < cur_os_time) {
60: 			return 0;
61: 		}
62: 		diff_ms = (uint32_t)(diff_time + base_os_time - cur_os_time);
63: 	} else {
64: 		uint64_t cur_os_time_64 = (0x100000000U + cur_os_time);
65: 		if((base_os_time + diff_time) < cur_os_time_64){
66: 			return 0;
67: 		}
68: 		diff_ms = (uint32_t)((base_os_time + diff_time) - cur_os_time_64);
69: 	}
70: 
71: 	if (diff_ms > 20000) {
72: 		BK_LOGD(TAG, "aon_rtc diff_ms: %dms.\r\n", diff_ms);
73: 		BK_LOGD(TAG, "cur aon time: 0x%x:0x%08x\r\n", (u32)(cur_aon_time >> 32), (u32)(cur_aon_time & 0xFFFFFFFF));
74: 	}
75: 
76: 	return  diff_ms / OS_MS_PER_TICK; // tick
77: #else
78: 	/* default to 1 tick */
79: 	return 1;
80: #endif
81: }

168: static inline void systick_update(TickType_t xExpectedIdleTime, uint32_t ulReloadValue)
169: {
170: 	uint32_t ulCompleteTickPeriods = 0, ulCompletedSysTickDecrements = 0;
171: 
172: 	/* Disable the SysTick clock without reading the
173: 	* portNVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL_REG register to ensure the
174: 	* portNVIC_SYSTICK_COUNT_FLAG_BIT is not cleared if it is set.
175: 	* Again, the time the SysTick is stopped for is accounted for as
176: 	* best it can be, but using the tickless mode will inevitably
177: 	* result in some tiny drift of the time maintained by the kernel
178: 	* with respect to calendar time*/
179: 	portNVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL_REG = ( portNVIC_SYSTICK_CLK_BIT | portNVIC_SYSTICK_INT_BIT );
180: 
181: 	/* Determine if the SysTick clock has already counted to zero and
182: 	* been set back to the current reload value (the reload back being
183: 	* correct for the entire expected idle time) or if the SysTick is
184: 	* yet to count to zero (in which case an interrupt other than the
185: 	* SysTick must have brought the system out of sleep mode). */
186: 	if( ( portNVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL_REG & portNVIC_SYSTICK_COUNT_FLAG_BIT ) != 0 ) {
187: 		uint32_t ulCalculatedLoadValue;
188: 		/* The tick interrupt is already pending, and the SysTick count
189: 		* reloaded with ulReloadValue.  Reset the
190: 		* portNVIC_SYSTICK_LOAD_REG with whatever remains of this tick
191: 		* period. */
192: 		ulCalculatedLoadValue = ( ulTimerCountsForOneTick - 1UL ) - ( ulReloadValue - portNVIC_SYSTICK_CURRENT_VALUE_REG );
193: 
194: 		/* Don't allow a tiny value, or values that have somehow
195: 		* underflowed because the post sleep hook did something
196: 		* that took too long. */
197: 		if( ( ulCalculatedLoadValue < ulStoppedTimerCompensation ) || ( ulCalculatedLoadValue > ulTimerCountsForOneTick ) ) {
198: 			ulCalculatedLoadValue = ( ulTimerCountsForOneTick - 1UL );
199: 		}
200: 
201: 		portNVIC_SYSTICK_LOAD_REG = ulCalculatedLoadValue;
202: 
203: 		/* As the pending tick will be processed as soon as this
204: 		* function exits, the tick value maintained by the tick is
205: 		* stepped forward by one less than the time spent waiting. */
206: 		ulCompleteTickPeriods = xExpectedIdleTime - 1UL;
207: 	} else {
208: 
209: 		/* Something other than the tick interrupt ended the sleep.
210: 		* Work out how long the sleep lasted rounded to complete tick
211: 		* periods (not the ulReload value which accounted for part
212: 		* ticks). */
213: 		ulCompletedSysTickDecrements = ( xExpectedIdleTime * ulTimerCountsForOneTick ) - portNVIC_SYSTICK_CURRENT_VALUE_REG;
214: 
215: 		/* How many complete tick periods passed while the processor
216: 		* was waiting? */
217: 		ulCompleteTickPeriods = ulCompletedSysTickDecrements / ulTimerCountsForOneTick;
218: 
219: 		/* The reload value is set to whatever fraction of a single tick
220: 		* period remains. */
221: 		portNVIC_SYSTICK_LOAD_REG = ( ( ulCompleteTickPeriods + 1UL ) * ulTimerCountsForOneTick ) - ulCompletedSysTickDecrements;
222: 	}
223: 
224: 	/* Restart SysTick so it runs from portNVIC_SYSTICK_LOAD_REG
225: 	* again, then set portNVIC_SYSTICK_LOAD_REG back to its standard
226: 	* value. */
227: 	portNVIC_SYSTICK_CURRENT_VALUE_REG = 0UL;
228: 	portNVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL_REG |= portNVIC_SYSTICK_ENABLE_BIT;
229: 
230: 	if (ulCompleteTickPeriods > 0) {
231: 		vTaskStepTick( ulCompleteTickPeriods );
232: 	}
233: 
234: 	portNVIC_SYSTICK_LOAD_REG = ulTimerCountsForOneTick - 1UL;
235: }
236: #endif

102:  *   of the initialization of the OS, just before beginning normal
103:  *   multitasking, the additional CPUs would be started by calling this
104:  *   function.
105:  *
106:  * Input Parameters:
107:  *   None
108:  *
109:  * Returned Value:
110:  *   Zero on success; a negated errno value on failure.
111:  *
112:  * Assumption:
113:  *   Runs before the full initialization sequence has completed.  Runs after
114:  *   all OS facilities are set up, but before multi-tasking has been started.
115:  *
116:  ****************************************************************************/
117: 
118: int nx_smp_start(void)
119: {
120:   int ret;
121:   int cpu;
122: 
123:   /* Flush dcache before start other CPUs. */
124: 
125:   up_flush_dcache_all();
126: 
127:   /* Start all of the other CPUs.  CPU0 is already running. */
128: 
129:   for (cpu = 1; cpu < CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS; cpu++)
130:     {
131:       /* Start the CPU */
132: 
133:       ret = up_cpu_start(cpu);
134:       if (ret < 0)
135:         {
136:           serr("ERROR: Failed to start CPU%d: %d\n", cpu, ret);
137:           return ret;
138:         }
139:     }
140: 
141:   return OK;

177:  *

179:  *   SMP function call handler
180:  *
181:  * Input Parameters:

191: int nxsched_smp_call_handler(int irq, FAR void *context,
192:                              FAR void *arg)
193: {
194:   FAR sq_queue_t *call_queue;
195:   FAR sq_entry_t *curr;
196:   FAR sq_entry_t *next;
197:   int cpu = this_cpu();
198: 
199:   irqstate_t flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&g_smp_call_lock);
200: 
201:   call_queue = &g_smp_call_queue[cpu];
202: 
203:   sq_for_every_safe(call_queue, curr, next)
204:     {
205:       FAR struct smp_call_data_s *data =
206:         container_of(curr, struct smp_call_data_s, node[cpu]);
207:       FAR struct smp_call_cookie_s *cookie;
208:       int ret;
209: 
210:       sq_rem(&data->node[cpu], call_queue);
211: 
212:       spin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_smp_call_lock, flags);
213: 
214:       ret = data->func(data->arg);
215: 
216:       flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&g_smp_call_lock);
217: 
218:       cookie = data->cookie;
219:       if (cookie != NULL)
220:         {
221:           if (ret < 0)
222:             {
223:               cookie->error = ret;
224:             }
225: 
226:           /* Insert ack back to original cpu call queue,
227:            * add direct avoid nxsched_smp_call_add g_smp_call_lock again.
228:            */
229: 
230: #if CONFIG_SMP_CALL_POOL_COUNT > 0
231:           sq_addlast(&cookie->ack.node[cookie->cpu],
232:                      &g_smp_call_queue[cookie->cpu]);
233:           up_send_smp_call(1 << cookie->cpu);
234: #else
235:           nxsem_post(&cookie->sem);
236: #endif
237:         }
238:     }
239: 
240:   spin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_smp_call_lock, flags);
241:   return OK;
242: }

113: static int ipc_heartbeat_timeout(void)
114: {
115: 	u32   cur_time;
116: 
117: 	cur_time = (u32)rtos_get_time();
118: 
119: 	if(cpu_x_state == CORE_POWER_OFF)
120: 	{
121: 		return 0;
122: 	}
123: 	if((cpu_x_state == CORE_STARTING) || (cpu_x_dump != 0))
124: 	{
125: 		cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp = cur_time;
126: 		return 0;
127: 	}
128: 
129: 	if(cur_time >= cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp)
130: 	{
131: 		cur_time -= cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp;
132: 	}
133: 	else
134: 	{
135: 		cur_time += (~(cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp)) + 1;  // wrap around.
136: 	}
137: 
138: 	if(cur_time < HB_TIMEOUT_MS)
139: 	{
140: 		cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp = (u32)rtos_get_time();
141: 		return 0;
142: 	}
143: 
144: 	if (bk_pm_module_lv_sleep_state_get(PM_DEV_ID_DEFAULT))
145: 	{
146: 		cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp = (u32)rtos_get_time();
147: 		bk_pm_module_lv_sleep_state_clear(PM_DEV_ID_DEFAULT);
148: 		return 0;
149: 	}
150: 
151: 	if(s_mb_ipc_work_state == MB_IPC_EXIT_LV)
152: 	{
153: 		cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp = (u32)rtos_get_time();
154: 		s_mb_ipc_work_state = MB_IPC_WORKING;
155: 		return 0;
156: 	}
157: 
158: 	return 1;
159: }

219: static void mb_ipc_task( void *para )
220: {
221: 	bk_err_t	ret_val;
222: 	u32    events;
223: 	u32    check_time = BEKEN_WAIT_FOREVER;
224: 
225: 	mb_ipc_init_lv_callback();
226: 
227: 	ret_val = rtos_init_event_ex(&mb_ipc_heart_event);
228: 
229: 	if(ret_val != BK_OK)
230: 	{
231: 		rtos_delete_thread(NULL);
232: 		return;
233: 	}
234: 
235: 	while(1)
236: 	{
237: 		events = rtos_wait_event_ex(&mb_ipc_heart_event, MB_IPC_ALL_FLAGS, true, check_time);
238: 
239: 		if(events == 0)
240: 		{
241: 			// timeout, so check heartbeat.
242: 			events = MB_IPC_HEARTBEAT_FLAG;
243: 		}
244: 
245: 		if(events & MB_IPC_STOP_CORE_FLAG)  // process this event at first!!!!
246: 		{
247: 			if(cpu_x_state == CORE_POWER_OFF)
248: 			{
249: 				events = 0;  // clear all events.
250: 			}
251: 		}
252: 
253: 		if(events & MB_IPC_START_CORE_FLAG)
254: 		{
255: 			u8   retry_cnt = 0;
256: 
257: 			while(cpu_x_state == CORE_STARTING)
258: 			{
259: 				ipc_heartbeat_timeout();
260: 
261: 				if(events & MB_IPC_POWER_UP_FLAG)
262: 				{
263: 					if(cpu_x_state == CORE_STARTING)
264: 					{
265: 						cpu_x_state = CORE_POWER_ON;
266: 						break;  // cpu1 power on.
267: 					}
268: 				}
269: 				else
270: 				{
271: 					if( retry_cnt > 3)
272: 					{
273: 						BK_DUMP_OUT("IPC retry to start core%d, retry_cnt:%d\r\n", cpu_x_id, retry_cnt);
274: 						// restart_cpu_x();
275: 						break;
276: 					}
277: 					else
278: 					{
279: 						events = rtos_wait_event_ex(&mb_ipc_heart_event, MB_IPC_POWER_UP_FLAG, true, 2000);//2s
280: 					}
281: 				}
282: 
283: 				retry_cnt++;
284: 			}
285: 
286: 			// discard this event when not in CORE_STARTING state.
287: 		}
288: 
289: 		if(events & MB_IPC_HEARTBEAT_FLAG)
290: 		{
291: 			if(ipc_heartbeat_timeout())

295: 				cpu_x_heartbeat_timeout = 1;
296: 				ap_console_bridge_link_down();
297: 				BK_ASSERT(false);
298: 			}
299: 		}

83: 	/* tx cmd data */
84: 	beken_semaphore_t	rsp_sema;

86: 	u8				tx_cmd;
87: 	volatile u8		tx_cmd_in_process;
88: 	volatile u8		tx_cmd_failed;
89: 	u32				rsp_buf[IPC_XCHG_DATA_MAX / sizeof(u32)];
90: 	u16				rsp_len;

94: 	u8			*	rx_xchg_buff;
95: 	u8				rx_cmd;
96: 	volatile u8		rx_cmd_in_process;

105: static inline uint32_t ipc_enter_critical()
106: {
107: 	uint32_t flags = rtos_disable_int();
108: 
109: #ifdef CONFIG_SOC_SMP
110: 	spin_lock(&mb_ipc_spin_lock);
111: #endif // CONFIG_SOC_SMP
112:

114: }

117: {
118: #ifdef CONFIG_SOC_SMP
119: 	spin_unlock(&mb_ipc_spin_lock);
120: #endif // CONFIG_SOC_SMP
121: 
122: 	rtos_enable_int(flags);
123: }

125: static void ipc_cmd_rx_isr(ipc_chnl_cb_t *chnl_cb, mb_chnl_cmd_t *cmd_buf)
126: {
127: 	u32		result = ACK_STATE_FAIL;
128: 	mb_chnl_ack_t * ack_buf = (mb_chnl_ack_t *)cmd_buf;
129: 	ipc_cmd_t     * ipc_cmd = (ipc_cmd_t *)cmd_buf;
130: 
131: 	/* chnl_cb->rx_xchg_buff == ipc_cmd->cmd_buff. MUST be true. */
132: 
133: 	if(cmd_buf->hdr.cmd & IPC_RSP_CMD_FLAG)  /* ipc rsp from other CPU. */
134: 	{
135: 		if(chnl_cb->tx_cmd_in_process == 0)	/* unsolicited ipc response. */
136: 		{
137: 			goto ipc_cmd_rx_isr_exit;
138: 		}
139: 
140: 		if(chnl_cb->tx_cmd != (cmd_buf->hdr.cmd & IPC_RSP_CMD_MASK))
141: 		{
142: 			/* un-matched rpc response. */
143: 			goto ipc_cmd_rx_isr_exit;
144: 		}
145: 
146: 		/* communication ok, function is completed. */
147: 		chnl_cb->tx_cmd_failed = 0;
148: 		chnl_cb->tx_cmd_in_process = 0;
149: 
150: 		BK_LOGD(MOD_TAG, "IPC_RSP_CMD: %d, %d, %d\r\n", cmd_buf->param1, cmd_buf->param2, cmd_buf->param3);
151: 
152: 		if(ipc_cmd->cmd_data_len > sizeof(chnl_cb->rsp_buf))
153: 		{
154: 			/* buffer insufficient, failed. */
155: 			chnl_cb->tx_cmd_failed = 1;
156: 			chnl_cb->rsp_len = 0;
157: 		}
158: 		else
159: 		{
160: 			/* returns ACK_STATE_COMPLETE,
161: 			   so must copy data from cmd_buff in case that the buffer is released. */
162: 			if((ipc_cmd->cmd_buff != NULL) && (ipc_cmd->cmd_data_len > 0))
163: 			{
164: 				#if CONFIG_CACHE_ENABLE
165: 				flush_dcache(ipc_cmd->cmd_buff, ipc_cmd->cmd_data_len);
166: 				#endif
167: 				__DMB();
168: 
169: 				memcpy(chnl_cb->rsp_buf, ipc_cmd->cmd_buff, ipc_cmd->cmd_data_len);
170: 
171: 				chnl_cb->rsp_len = ipc_cmd->cmd_data_len;
172: 			}
173: 			else
174: 			{
175: 				chnl_cb->rsp_len = 0;
176: 			}
177: 		}
178: 
179: 		rtos_set_semaphore(&chnl_cb->rsp_sema);
180: 
181: 		ipc_rsp_t * ipc_rsp = (ipc_rsp_t *)ack_buf;
182: 
183: 		/* it is a rsp command, nothing need to be returned. */
184: 		ipc_rsp->rsp_buff = NULL;
185: 		ipc_rsp->rsp_data_len = 0;
186: 
187: 		result = ACK_STATE_COMPLETE;
188: 
189: 		goto ipc_cmd_rx_isr_exit;
190: 	}
191: 	else
192: 	{
193: 		chnl_cb->rx_cmd = cmd_buf->hdr.cmd;
194: 		chnl_cb->rx_cmd_in_process = 1;
195: 
196: 		BK_LOGV(MOD_TAG, "IPC_CMD: %d, %d, %d\r\n", cmd_buf->param1, cmd_buf->param2, cmd_buf->param3);
197: 
198: 		if(ipc_cmd->cmd_data_len > sizeof(chnl_cb->cmd_buf))
199: 		{
200: 			result = ACK_STATE_FAIL;
201: 		}
202: 		else
203: 		{
204: 			/* may return ACK_STATE_COMPLETE,
205: 			   so must copy data from cmd_buff in case that the buffer is released. */
206: 			if((ipc_cmd->cmd_buff != NULL) && (ipc_cmd->cmd_data_len > 0))
207: 			{
208: 				#if CONFIG_CACHE_ENABLE
209: 				flush_dcache(ipc_cmd->cmd_buff, ipc_cmd->cmd_data_len);
210: 				#endif
211: 				__DMB();
212: 
213: 				memcpy(chnl_cb->cmd_buf, ipc_cmd->cmd_buff, ipc_cmd->cmd_data_len);
214: 
215: 				chnl_cb->cmd_len = ipc_cmd->cmd_data_len;
216: 			}
217: 			else
218: 			{
219: 				chnl_cb->cmd_len = 0;
220: 			}

17: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_REENTER     0xa2000000u
18: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_OWNER_BUSY  0xa3000000u
19: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_INTENT      0xa4000000u
20: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_CONFLICT    0xa5000000u
21: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ACQUIRED    0xa6000000u
22: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_UNLOCK      0xa7000000u

26: {
27:   volatile uint32_t interested[2];
28:   volatile uint32_t turn;
29:   volatile uint32_t owner;
30:   volatile uint32_t depth;
31: };
32: 
33: static struct bk7258_atomic_gate_s g_bk7258_atomic_gate
34:   __attribute__((section(".bk_spinlock"), aligned(32)));

36: static inline void bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(unsigned int cpu, uint32_t value)
37: {
38:   if (cpu == 0 &&
39:       bk7258_boottrace_primary_stage() == BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_FIRST_IRQ)
40:     {
41:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(4, value);
42:     }
43: }

45: static bool bk7258_hwspinlock_trylock(struct hwspinlock_dev_s *dev)
46: {
47:   unsigned int cpu = (unsigned int)up_cpu_index();
48:   unsigned int other = cpu ^ 1u;
49: 
50:   (void)dev;
51:   DEBUGASSERT(cpu < 2);
52:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ENTRY);
53: 
54:   /* BK7258 has only two SRAM exclusive monitors while CP, AP CPU1 and AP
55:    * CPU2 are all active.  Keep the AP-only atomic gate independent of
56:    * LDAEX/STREX so CP traffic cannot starve an AP exclusive sequence.
57:    */
58: 
59:   /* libc atomics are normally short, but the scheduler's recursive critical
60:    * section can issue another atomic operation on the same CPU.  Re-entry
61:    * must be decided before entering Peterson arbitration; otherwise a waiter
62:    * on the other CPU can make the current owner wait for itself.
63:    */
64: 
65:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner == cpu + 1u)
66:     {
67:       if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth == UINT32_MAX)
68:         {
69:           PANIC();
70:         }
71: 
72:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth++;
73:       UP_DMB();
74:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_REENTER |
75:                              g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth);
76:       return true;
77:     }
78: 
79:   /* This is only a fast rejection.  The Peterson protocol below remains
80:    * authoritative while a new owner is between intent and owner publish.
81:    */
82: 
83:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner != 0)
84:     {
85:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_OWNER_BUSY |
86:                              g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner);
87:       return false;
88:     }
89: 
90:   /* Every attempt must publish a fresh intent and turn.  Leaving intent set
91:    * after a failed trylock makes the state stale and breaks trylock's
92:    * one-attempt contract.
93:    */
94: 
95:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[cpu] = 1;
96:   UP_DMB();
97:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.turn = other;
98:   UP_DMB();
99:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_INTENT);
100: 
101:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[other] != 0 &&
102:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.turn == other)
103:     {
104:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[cpu] = 0;
105:       UP_DMB();
106:       __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
107:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_CONFLICT);
108:       return false;
109:     }
110: 
111:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner = cpu + 1u;
112:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth = 1;
113:   UP_DMB();
114:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ACQUIRED);
115:   return true;
116: }
117: 
118: static void bk7258_hwspinlock_relax(struct hwspinlock_dev_s *dev)
119: {
120:   (void)dev;
121:   __asm__ volatile("nop" ::: "memory");
122: }
123: 
124: static void bk7258_hwspinlock_unlock(struct hwspinlock_dev_s *dev)
125: {
126:   unsigned int cpu = (unsigned int)up_cpu_index();
127: 
128:   (void)dev;
129:   if (cpu >= 2 || g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner != cpu + 1u ||
130:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth == 0)
131:     {
132:       PANIC();
133:     }
134: 
135:   if (--g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth != 0)
136:     {
137:       UP_DMB();
138:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_UNLOCK |
139:                              g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth);
140:       return;
141:     }
142: 
143:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner = 0;
144:   UP_DMB();
145:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[cpu] = 0;
146:   UP_DSB();
147:   __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
148:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_RELEASED);
149: }

155:   .unlock  = bk7258_hwspinlock_unlock
156: };

448:       sched_lock();

453:       ret = data->func(data->arg);
454:       if (data->cookie != NULL)
455:         {
456:           data->cookie->error = ret;
457:           nxsem_post(&data->cookie->sem);
458:           if (ret < 0)
459:             {
460:               goto out;
461:             }
462:         }
463: 
464:       CPU_CLR(this_cpu(), &cpuset);
465:     }
466: 
467:   cpucnt = CPU_COUNT(&cpuset);

469:     {
470:       goto out;
471:     }
472: 
473:   for (i = 0; i < CONFIG_NCPUS; i++)

<thinking>**Synthesizing behavior differences****Checking current implementation source status and no modifications****Preparing final report with exact lines**## Scope and terminology

I treated the vendor Armino/FreeRTOS AP as the reference implementation and the OpenVela tree as the current implementation:

- Original/vendor reference:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/`
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/`
- Current OpenVela implementation:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/`
  - Board-specific code under `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/`

The BK vendor naming is slightly confusing:

- Vendor logical CPU0 is the primary AP core.
- Vendor logical CPU1 is the secondary AP core used by FreeRTOS SMP.
- The vendor `CPU2_CORE_ID` is a separate physical core path and is compiled only when `CONFIG_CPU_CNT > 2`.
- Current OpenVela has exactly two AP logical CPUs: NuttX CPU0 and NuttX CPU1. The current `CPU2` terminology in the source refers to the physical BK7258 secondary AP core, while NuttX calls it logical CPU1.

The current log is:

```text
primary=26 secondary=10 detail3=2 detail4=a8000000
```

The five CP-reported detail words are actually trace slots 3 through 7. Therefore:

```text
detail3 = trace[5] = 0x00000002
detail4 = trace[6] = 0xa8000000
```

This is not the same as `detail[2]` or `detail[3]` in the OpenVela README’s prose. The exact slot mapping is defined by `bk7258_boottrace_detail()` at `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/include/bk7258_boottrace.h:76-85`, where `detail(index, value)` stores at `trace[index + 3]`.

---

# 1. Vendor/original FreeRTOS startup

## 1.1 Primary CPU starts the scheduler and releases the secondary AP core

The vendor FreeRTOS SMP scheduler starts on logical CPU0. `xPortStartScheduler()`:

1. Validates that it is running on CPU0.
2. Sets `ucPrimaryCoreNum = configTICK_CORE`.
3. Initializes the cross-core mailbox.
4. Calls `multicore_launch_core1()`.
5. Delays with a fixed busy loop.
6. Starts the scheduler on the primary core.

Citations:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/os_source/freertos_smp_v2p0/FreeRTOS-Kernel/portable/GCC/ARM_CM33_NTZ/non_secure/port.c:1202-1225`
- The same implementation is present in the preserved original tree:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/os_source/freertos_smp_v2p0/FreeRTOS-Kernel/portable/GCC/ARM_CM33_NTZ/non_secure/port.c:1202-1225`

The relevant vendor code is:

```c
ucPrimaryCoreNum = configTICK_CORE;
configASSERT(portGET_CORE_ID() == 0);
bk_mailbox_cc_init();
multicore_launch_core1(prvDisableInterruptsAndPortStartSchedulerOnCore);
for (volatile uint32_t i = 0; i < 1000000; i++);
xPortStartSchedulerOnCore();
```

The fixed delay is explicitly described as avoiding the primary scheduler starting before the other core has completed enough startup, rather than as a handshake:

```c
for(volatile uint32_t i = 0; i < 1000000; i++);
```

There is no vendor equivalent of the current OpenVela hardware FIFO `BOOT_NOTIFY → BOOT_PING → BOOT_ACK` transaction.

## 1.2 Reset/vector programming for physical CPU1/CPU2

The vendor reset functions program the secondary physical core’s power, reset, RX-event selection, and boot-vector offset:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_startup/system_main.c:174-183`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_startup/system_main.c:205-214`

For the physical secondary AP core:

```c
sys_drv_set_cpu2_pwr_dw(0);
sys_drv_set_cpu2_rxevt_sel(1);
sys_drv_set_cpu2_boot_address_offset(offset >> 8);
sys_drv_set_cpu2_reset(start_flag);
```

The vendor FreeRTOS SMP launch path passes the address of the CPU1 vector table to the physical CPU2 reset control:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/cmsis/CMSIS_5/Device/Beken/bk7236xx/Source/smp/startup_cpu1.c:252-267`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/cmsis/CMSIS_5/Device/Beken/bk7236xx/Source/smp/startup_cpu2.c:241-258`

The CPU1 launch function is:

```c
void multicore_launch_core1(void (*func)(void))
{
    multicore_cpu1_func = func;
    reset_cpu2_core((uint32_t)&__vector_core1_table, 1);
}
```

The CPU2 launch function, enabled only for a third configured core, is:

# 3. Current OpenVela CPU2 startup

## 3.1 CPU2 reset/vector programming is explicit and hardware-verified

Current OpenVela uses a dedicated two-entry secondary vector table:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_vectors.c:54-61`

```c

  __attribute__((used, section(".bk_secondary_vectors"), aligned(512))) =
{
  (vector_t)__secondary_boot_stack_top,
  bk7258_secondary_start
};
```

The secondary physical CPU is held and released through explicit CPU2 control bits:

- Hold:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpustart.c:44-49`
- Release:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpustart.c:51-57`

```c
putreg32(getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL) & ~RESET_RELEASE,
         BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL);
...
putreg32(getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL) | RESET_RELEASE,
         BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL);
```

Before release, OpenVela:

1. Verifies CPU2 power/run status.
2. Holds CPU2 in reset.
3. Verifies reset hold through control and run-status readback.
4. Clears CPU2 interrupt enables.
5. Programs the CPU2 RX-event selection and vector offset.
6. Flushes barriers.
7. Saves CPU0 interrupt state.
8. Releases CPU2 reset.

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpustart.c:147-191`

```c

            BK7258_CPU2_RXEVT_SEL |
            (((uintptr_t)__secondary_vectors_start >> 8) <<
             BK7258_CPU2_OFFSET_SHIFT));
```

This is more defensive than the vendor path, which writes the boot offset and reset bit but does not perform the same post-write status verification or handshake validation.

## 3.2 Current secondary entry starts with interrupts disabled

Current secondary entry is a naked function:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpustart.c:116-129`

This assigns logical NuttX CPU1 by writing `1` to the CPU-ID location, establishes the bootstrap stack limit, and branches directly into C startup while global interrupts are still disabled.

2. Secondary NVIC initialization.

## 3.3 Current secondary ordering: stack, online, notify, then interrupt enable

The current secondary idle handoff is:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpustart.c:59-71`

```c

bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ONLINE);

bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_NOTIFY);
```

This ordering is intentional:

2. Publish the secondary as online.
3. Send the raw boot notification.

This is important for the current log because `secondary=10` proves the secondary reached the ACK stage after this ordering, not merely that it entered the secondary reset handler.

Current OpenVela separates the boot handshake from the normal scheduler/call IPI state machine:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_smpcall.c:22-31`

# 6. Ready IPC sent to CP

## 6.1 Original vendor CP contract

The original vendor CP recognizes `PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY_CMD = 0x5`:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/include/driver/pwr_clk.h:25-34`

```c

```

The CP receives it in the PM mailbox ISR and changes its CPU1 boot-ready state:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:209-248`

```c
case PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY_CMD:
    if (cmd_buf->param1 == 0x1)
        s_pm_cp1_boot_ready = PM_MAILBOX_COMMUNICATION_FINISH;
    else
        s_pm_cp1_boot_ready = PM_MAILBOX_COMMUNICATION_INIT;
```

The vendor AP’s heartbeat/IPC mechanism is initialized during CP startup and is based on reset notifications, power-on notifications, and periodic heartbeat messages:

- CP initialization:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/bk_startup/system_main.c:565-568`
- AP reset notification:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_startup/system_main.c:185-201`
- AP heartbeat implementation:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_heartbeat.c:249-295`

The vendor heartbeat implementation does not wait for a CPU2 boot ACK before the boot-ready IPC. It treats the reset/power-on notification as the beginning of a `CORE_STARTING` state and waits for a power-up event.

The original AP implementation permits only one retry wait in the equivalent code:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_heartbeat.c:200-224`

```c
if (retry_cnt > 0)
{
    BK_LOGE(...);
    break;
}
else
{
    events = rtos_wait_event_ex(..., 2000);
}
retry_cnt++;
```

The current `bk_avdk_smp` tree has a slightly different version allowing retries through `retry_cnt > 3`:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_heartbeat.c:253-284`

but both implementations are still event/timer-based and do not constitute a CPU2 hardware FIFO boot proof.

## 6.2 Current OpenVela ready sequence

Current OpenVela preserves the existing `0x5` command, but moves it to a later, explicit milestone:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_pwc.c:511-554`

The current sequence is:

1. Initialize PM queues/semaphores.
2. Register the PWC receive callback.
3. Send `PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY_CMD (0x5)` with `param1=1`.
4. Wait for the CP transport acknowledgement.
5. Record `BK7258_BOOT_READY_SENT`.

```c
ret = pwc_send_wait(PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY_CMD, 1, 0, 0);
...
bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_READY_SENT);
```

The OpenVela README describes the semantic change:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/README.md:321-336`

`0x5` now only releases the CP boot worker’s wait. It is not the final OpenVela PWC/bridge-ready indication. A separate `PM_OPENVELA_READY_CMD = 0x11` is used for the final commit.

The constants are defined at:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_pwc.c:24-35`

```c
#define PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY_CMD 0x5u
#define PM_OPENVELA_READY_CMD 0x11u
```

This is a major behavioral difference from the original vendor expectation: the current OpenVela `0x5` is sent only after SMP bring-up has progressed through the new handshake and later board bring-up gates, and final readiness is separately committed.

# 7. Boot retry and failure behavior

## 7.1 Vendor retry behavior

There are several independent vendor retry/failure mechanisms:

### Scheduler startup delay

The FreeRTOS primary core uses a fixed busy-loop delay rather than a positive secondary-core acknowledgement:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/os_source/freertos_smp_v2p0/FreeRTOS-Kernel/portable/GCC/ARM_CM33_NTZ/non_secure/port.c:1215-1222`

```c
multicore_launch_core1(...);
for (volatile uint32_t i = 0; i < 1000000; i++);
xPortStartSchedulerOnCore();
```

### IPC start wait

The heartbeat task waits for a power-up event in 2-second intervals and gives up after the configured retry threshold:

- Original backup:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp_original_backup/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_heartbeat.c:253-284`
- Current vendor tree:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_heartbeat.c:253-284`

### Heartbeat timeout

After startup, a missed heartbeat eventually results in an assertion:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_heartbeat.c:289-299`

```c
BK_LOGE(... "heartbeat timeout");
ap_console_bridge_link_down();
BK_ASSERT(false);
```

The vendor code contains commented-out `restart_cpu_x()` calls rather than a robust boot rollback path:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_heartbeat.c:161-178`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_heartbeat.c:271-275`

## 7.2 Current OpenVela retry behavior

Current OpenVela has two different retry scopes.

### Raw boot mailbox retry

Boot-only mailbox commands retry up to 1024 attempts when the FIFO returns `-EAGAIN`:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_smpcall.c:22-61`

```c
#define BK7258_IPI_RETRY_LIMIT 1024
...
for (retry = 0; retry < BK7258_IPI_RETRY_LIMIT; retry++)
```

Normal scheduler/call IPI sends use the same bounded retry loop and clear `g_ipi_kicked` on failure:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_smpcall.c:63-100`

### CPU2 online/ACK timeout

`up_cpu_start()` waits for the complete notify/ACK handshake for either:

- half a second at 480 MHz, or
- a 4,000,000-iteration polling limit,

whichever comes first:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpustart.c:38-40`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpustart.c:193-212`

If the handshake fails, OpenVela:

1. Saves CPU control/status/FIFO diagnostics.
2. Reasserts CPU2 reset.
3. Restores CPU0 interrupt state.
4. Logs the timeout.
5. Calls `PANIC()`.

Citations:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpustart.c:214-230`

This is materially different from the vendor fixed delay and commented-out restart logic.

### CP boot timeout and rollback

The CP-side OpenVela lifecycle has a longer AP boot deadline and a rollback path:

- Timeout logging:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:634-658`
- OpenVela README description:
  - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/README.md:330-336`

The current CP logic no longer turns a stage-4 timeout directly into an unconditional whole-chip reset. It retains diagnostics and performs rollback. The final OpenVela-ready commit is separately gated.

# 8. Exact interpretation of `primary=26 secondary=10 detail3=2 detail4=a8000000`

## 8.1 `primary=26`

The primary stage constants are:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/include/bk7258_boottrace.h:27-35`

```c
#define BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_ENTER       20u
#define BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_HELD        21u
#define BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_RELEASED    22u
#define BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_ONLINE      23u
#define BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_IPI_DONE   24u
#define BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_IRQ_RESTORE 25u
#define BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_FIRST_IRQ   26u
#define BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_IRQ_RETURN  27u
#define BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_START_DONE  28u
```

At primary stage 26, the current CPU0 has restored or is restoring interrupts and has entered its first interrupt. The exact transition is recorded by `arm_ack_irq()`:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_irq.c:235-243`

```c
if (up_cpu_index() == 0 &&
    bk7258_boottrace_primary_stage() == BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_IRQ_RESTORE)
{
    bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, (uint32_t)irq);
    bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_FIRST_IRQ);
}
```

Thus the observed `primary=26` says:

- CPU2 reset release succeeded.
- The CPU2 secondary reached the boot handshake.
- CPU0 received the expected ACK.
- CPU0 got as far as restoring its interrupt state and taking its first interrupt.
- `up_cpu_start()` did not yet reach stage 27/28.

## 8.2 `secondary=10`

Secondary stage 10 is `BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ACK`:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/include/bk7258_boottrace.h:42-51`

```c
#define BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ACK 10u
```

It is written when CPU1 receives `BOOT_PING` and sends `BOOT_ACK`:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_smpcall.c:117-126`

Therefore `secondary=10` proves the physical secondary CPU:

1. Entered the secondary vector.
2. Initialized private CPU state.
3. Initialized its NVIC.
4. Initialized its mailbox.
5. Set up its stack.
6. Published online.
7. Sent `BOOT_NOTIFY`.
8. Enabled interrupts.
9. Received CPU0’s `BOOT_PING`.
10. Sent `BOOT_ACK`.

It is stronger evidence than merely observing `secondary=9`, which would only prove global interrupts were enabled.

## 8.3 `detail3=2`

The detail slots are written by:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_timerisr.c:33-50`

```c
if (primary_stage == BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_FIRST_IRQ)
    bk7258_boottrace_detail(3, 1);

nxsched_process_timer();

if (primary_stage == BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_FIRST_IRQ)
    bk7258_boottrace_detail(3, 2);
```

Because trace detail index 3 is stored at trace word 6, the CP log’s `detail3=2` means:

```text
nxsched_process_timer() returned
```

However, there is an important limitation: in the actual logged format, confirm whether the CP’s “detail3” label is zero-based or one-based. The OpenVela trace array itself is unambiguous:

- `detail(3, 1)` means `trace[6] = 1`.
- `detail(3, 2)` means `trace[6] = 2`.

If the reported field `detail3` corresponds to `trace[6]`, then `detail3=2` means the timer core handler returned. If it instead means source-level `detail[3]`, that is the same conclusion.

The README documents the intended state machine:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/README.md:395-402`

```text
detail[3]=0: not yet in timer ISR
detail[3]=1: in timer ISR, executing nxsched_process_timer()
detail[3]=2: timer core processing returned
```

Therefore this log is later than the earlier observed `detail3=1` stop.

## 8.4 `detail4=0xa8000000`

The gate trace values are defined at:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_hwspinlock.c:16-23`

```c
#define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ENTRY       0xa1000000u
#define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_REENTER     0xa2000000u
#define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_OWNER_BUSY  0xa3000000u
#define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_INTENT      0xa4000000u
#define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_CONFLICT    0xa5000000u
#define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ACQUIRED    0xa6000000u
#define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_UNLOCK      0xa7000000u
#define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_RELEASED    0xa8000000u
```

`0xa8000000` is `BK7258_GATE_TRACE_RELEASED`.

The trace is written only when logical CPU0 is in primary stage 26:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_hwspinlock.c:36-43`

The release trace is emitted after:

1. Decrementing recursive depth to zero.
2. Clearing the owner.
3. Clearing the current CPU’s Peterson interest bit.
4. Executing a DSB.
5. Sending SEV.

Citations:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_hwspinlock.c:124-149`

Therefore `detail4=0xa8000000` means the CPU0 atomic gate was fully released during the first-interrupt/timer window. It does **not** indicate that the gate acquisition succeeded at the exact final instruction; it indicates that at least one complete gate release occurred.

The README warns that this is not sufficient to prove the scheduler completed:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/README.md:404-415`

In particular, `nxsched_process_timer()` calls `clock_timer()`, and the first atomic/seqlock path can be entered there. The current source’s trace value shows a release, but the actual halt could be in a subsequent atomic operation, scheduler critical section, or exception return path.

# 9. What the current log rules out

Given:

```text
primary=26 secondary=10 detail3=2 detail4=a8000000
```

The following earlier failure modes are ruled out:

- CPU0 never reached `bk7258_start()`.
- CPU0 stalled before BSS clearing.
- CPU0 failed to copy runtime vectors.
- CPU2 reset was never released.
- CPU2 never entered its vector.
- CPU2 never initialized its private state.
- CPU2 never initialized its NVIC.
- CPU2 never initialized its mailbox.
- CPU2 never sent `BOOT_NOTIFY`.
- CPU0 never sent `BOOT_PING`.
- CPU2 never sent `BOOT_ACK`.
- CPU0 never received the handshake ACK.
- CPU0 never restored interrupts.
- CPU0 never entered the first interrupt.
- CPU0 remained stuck inside the first `nxsched_process_timer()` call.

The log instead places the failure after:

```text
CPU2 ACK
→ CPU0 interrupt restore
→ first IRQ
→ timer ISR entry
→ nxsched_process_timer() return
→ at least one Peterson gate release
```

It does **not** prove that:

- the first interrupt was SysTick rather than another IRQ, unless the corresponding `detail[2]`/trace[5] value is also known;
- `up_irq_restore(flags)` returned;
- `up_cpu_start()` returned;
- NuttX reached normal scheduler execution on both CPUs;
- the CP received `PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY_CMD (0x5)`.

The next distinguishing diagnostic should be the IRQ number in trace word 5. `arm_ack_irq()` records it at detail index 2:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_irq.c:237-242`

The README documents the expected values:

- SysTick: IRQ 15
- Mailbox: IRQ 79

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/README.md:373-378`

If the corresponding IRQ is 15, the current log confirms the sequence has advanced through the first direct SysTick handler and returned from `nxsched_process_timer()`. If it is 79, the first interrupt is still mailbox-related, and the timer path is not necessarily implicated despite the `detail3=2` value.

## Bottom line

The vendor implementation uses:

```text
CPU0 scheduler start
→ program/release secondary reset/vector
→ ordinary mailbox setup
→ fixed busy-loop delay
→ both cores enter FreeRTOS scheduler
→ vStartFirstTask()
→ cpsie i
→ SVC
→ first task exception return
```

The current OpenVela implementation uses:

```text
CPU0 NuttX startup
→ explicit CPU2 reset hold/status verification
→ CPU2 vector/RX-event programming
→ raw CPU2 reset release
→ CPU2 private/NVIC/mailbox setup
→ CPU2 stack and online publication
→ CPU2 BOOT_NOTIFY
→ CPU0 actively drains FIFO
→ CPU0 BOOT_PING
→ CPU2 IRQ sends BOOT_ACK
→ CPU0 clears pending mailbox IRQ
→ restores CPU0 interrupts
→ first IRQ
→ direct CPU0-only SysTick
→ nxsched_process_timer()
```

The current log confirms that the new reset/vector/mailbox handshake is working. The remaining failure is in or immediately after the first interrupt/timer/scheduler transition, not in physical CPU2 reset release or the CPU2 mailbox boot handshake.
